claims.explanation: Mocetinostat is a class I HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity likely reflects dependence on HDAC1/2/3-mediated epigenetic silencing and intact apoptotic/antigen-presentation programs. Sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 mutation, EGFR/BRAF/PIK3CA-driven oncogenic signaling, and SWI/SNF/COMPASS chromatin-modifier mutations, whereas resistant lines often retain wild-type TP53 or have alterations such as MAP2K1, VHL, or EP300 that may blunt HDAC-inhibitor responses. High HDAC1/2/3 expression and ZEB1-driven EMT would further predict sensitivity.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in selectively killed lines, consistent with loss of p53-mediated survival after HDAC inhibition
Mocetinostat targets HDAC1; higher target expression predicts greater dependence and drug effect
Mocetinostat targets HDAC2; class I HDAC activity is associated with malignant gene repression
Mocetinostat targets HDAC3; class I HDAC inhibition restores silenced genes
ZEB1-driven EMT and stemness confer resistance that mocetinostat reverses via class I HDAC inhibition
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PIK3CA mutations appear in several selectively killed gastric, colorectal, and ovarian lines
SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling mutations may increase epigenetic drug dependence
COMPASS chromatin-modifier mutations are enriched in sensitive lines
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the least affected lines
VHL-mutant 786O kidney line is among the least affected lines
